cohort: Participants were 448 women admitted to the maternal intensive care unit of El-Shatby University Hospital in Alexandria, Egypt, who fulfilled WHO criteria for maternal near-miss during 2014.
finding: Low maternal education and inadequate antenatal care were significantly associated with maternal mortality, with severe pre-eclampsia and post-partum hemorrhage being the most common causes for intensive care unit admission, while sepsis and multiple organ dysfunction were significant predictors of maternal mortality.
